name: Oklahoma

notes: Groceries are exempt from the 4.5% state tax since August 29, 2024 (House Bill 1955); city and county taxes still apply at their full rate.

Alcohol bought in stores: beer, wine and spirits bought at stores pay the sales tax, on top of excise taxes left out here (spirits $1.47 a liter, wine 19 cents a liter, sparkling wine 55 cents, strong beer $12.50 a barrel). Drinks served in bars and restaurants also pay a 13.5% mixed beverage gross receipts tax, counted for drinks served.

Drinks served pay the sales tax plus the 13.5% mixed beverage gross receipts tax, on liquor, wine and beer alike, including at restaurants with only an on-premises beer and wine license (37A O.S. 5-105(A), since October 1, 2018).

Cigarettes and other tobacco pay no state or local sales tax: State Question 713 (2004) replaced it with a higher excise tax ($2.03 a pack of cigarettes today), left out here. Vapor products appear still to pay the sales tax (not verified), which is not counted here.
Barber and beauty services aren't taxed: shops are consumers of the supplies they use, and only products sold apart from the service are taxed.
Clothing is taxed. The 2026 sales tax holiday ran August 7 to 9 (clothing and footwear under $100).

Laundry and dry cleaning: laundering and dry cleaning customers' clothing aren't taxed; linen, uniform and other rentals that include cleaning are taxed on the whole charge, which is not counted here.
Gasoline is exempt from the sales tax and pays a 19-cent-a-gallon state tax instead, left out here.
Auto repair labor: separately stated repair and installation labor isn't taxed; the parts are.
Diapers and menstrual products are taxed (a 2026 bill to exempt diapers did not pass).

Hotel stays pay the sales tax plus city lodging taxes (Oklahoma City's 9.25% since October 1, 2024; Tulsa's 5%; a rise to 9.9% was on the November 3, 2026 ballot, its result not yet read), which are not counted here.
Sales by tribal businesses on trust land are outside the state sales tax; tribes levy their own taxes, which are not counted here.
Oklahoma did not answer the 2017 FTA survey; it taxes only the services its law lists (68 O.S. 1354), and the services below are from state law and rules.
gaps: 37 cities lie in more than one county with a different rate in each county part; in each census tract such a city's rate is that of its part in the tract's county, counted for the share of the tract's store jobs located in the city.
Food and drug items carry a different rate here (state 0%), and a different local rate where the locality sets one. What counts as food follows the state's rules.
Selah, a McClain County town with a 4% sales tax since October 1, 2026, isn't a 2024 Census place, so its tracts take McClain County's rate (noted on the county's page).

Small parts of Mannford (in Pawnee and Tulsa counties), Okmulgee (Okfuskee County), Chattanooga (Tillman County) and Lindsay (McClain County) have no records in the state's rate files, so they aren't split out: census tracts there count each city's rate from its main county for the share of their store jobs located in the city.

Changes from January 1, 2027 aren't in the rates: Ottawa County (1.35% to 2.35%) and Hominy (3% to 4%). On November 3, 2026, Oklahoma County voted on a 0.4% county tax and Eufaula on a 1% city tax, both from April 1, 2027, and Tulsa on its hotel tax; their results haven't been read yet, and each is noted on its page.

4024650: A new 1% city sales tax for street improvements, from April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2042 (Ordinance 26-07-01; City of Eufaula election notice), was on Eufaula's November 3, 2026 ballot; its result hasn't been read yet. It isn't counted here.
4035850: Hominy's city sales tax rises from 3% to 4% on January 1, 2027 (Oklahoma Tax Commission); the change isn't in the rates here.
4065400: Sapulpa's Tulsa County part pays a 4.5% city rate, against 4% in Creek County (Oklahoma Tax Commission); the state's rate files give much of that part the 4% rate, so the Tax Commission's 4.867% local is used for it: census tracts in Tulsa County count it for the share of their store jobs located in Sapulpa (their residents' share where a tract has no store jobs), and Sapulpa's own page weighs its two parts by its store jobs in each.
4075000: Tulsa's voters were asked on November 3, 2026 about raising the city's hotel tax from 5% to 9.9% from January 1, 2027 (Tulsa City Council); the result hasn't been read yet, and lodging taxes aren't counted here.
40087: Selah, a town incorporated in McClain County, has levied a 4% sales tax since October 1, 2026 (Oklahoma Tax Commission). It isn't a 2024 Census place, so its tracts take McClain County's rate here.
40109: Oklahoma County's voters were asked on November 3, 2026 about a 0.4% county sales tax for the jail and mental health care, from April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2052 (as reported by News 9); its result hasn't been read yet, and it isn't counted here.
40115: Ottawa County's sales tax rises from 1.35% to 2.35% on January 1, 2027 (Oklahoma Tax Commission); the current 1.35% is used here.
